title: Invariant open image and its cartesian descended model
statement:
Let $q:W\to W'$ be a flat, quasi-compact, surjective morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Let $j:V\hookrightarrow W$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], put $O=j(|V|)\subseteq |W|$, and let $r_0,r_1:W\times_{W'}W\to W$ be the projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose $r_0^{-1}(O)=r_1^{-1}(O)$. Then, for any $x,y\in |W|$ with $q(x)=q(y)$, one has $x\in O\iff y\in O$. The subset $U=q(O)$ is open in $W'$, satisfies $q^{-1}(U)=O$, and is the unique subset of $|W'|$ with that inverse image. Giving $U$ its open-subscheme structure and writing $i:U\hookrightarrow W'$, there is a unique morphism $h:V\to U$ with $i\circ h=q\circ j$, and the square with sides $j,h,q,i$ is cartesian; equivalently, the canonical morphism $V\to W\times_{W'}U$ is an isomorphism compatible with $j$ and $h$.

Moreover, let $A\to B$ and $W'\to B$ be morphisms of schemes and let $\theta:W\simeq W'\times_B A$ identify $q$ with the projection to $W'$. Give $V$ the induced map to $A$. If $\phi$ is a descent datum on $V$ over $A/B$ [def-pd-descent-datum] and the open immersion $\theta\circ j$ intertwines $\phi$ with the canonical datum on $W'\times_B A$, then $h$ and $V\to A$ induce an isomorphism $V\simeq U\times_B A$ whose induced descent datum is exactly $\phi$. No quasi-affineness, quasi-compactness of $V$, or local finite-presentation hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image] to the kernel-pair square and the subset $O$: $r_1(r_0^{-1}(O))=q^{-1}(q(O))$. By the assumed equality of inverse images, its left side equals $r_1(r_1^{-1}(O))$, which is contained in $O$. Conversely $O\subseteq q^{-1}(q(O))$ for every function. Thus $q^{-1}(q(O))=O$. If $q(x)=q(y)$ and $x\in O$, then $q(y)\in q(O)$, hence $y\in O$; interchanging $x,y$ proves the equivalence. This uses the scheme fibre-product image formula, without identifying scheme points with pairs of points.

source.place: Tag 01S1, lemma-base-change-surjective, proof (subset image formula), applied to the kernel pair; Tag 0247 final paragraph in descent.tex

proof.text: Put $U=q(O)$. The open-immersion definition [def-weil-open-immersion] makes $O$ open. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-qc-surjective-quotient-map] to $q$, which is flat, quasi-compact and surjective by hypothesis: since $q^{-1}(U)=O$ is open, $U$ is open. If $T\subseteq |W^{\prime}|$ also has inverse image $O$, surjectivity gives $T=q(q^{-1}(T))=q(O)=U$. This proves uniqueness even among arbitrary subsets.

source.place: Tag 02JY, lemma-fpqc-quotient-topology; used in Tag 0247 final paragraph of descent.tex

proof.text: Equip $U$ with its open-subscheme structure. The image of $q\circ j$ is $q(O)=U$, so [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] supplies the unique $h:V\to U$ satisfying $i\circ h=q\circ j$.

source.place: Tag 01HI, lemma-restrict-map-to-opens; the open model in Tag 0247 final paragraph of descent.tex

proof.text: To verify the cartesian assertion directly, let $a:T\to W$ and $b:T\to U$ satisfy $q\circ a=i\circ b$. Every point of $a(T)$ belongs to $q^{-1}(U)=O$. By [def-weil-open-immersion], $j$ identifies $V$ with the open subscheme on $O$, so [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] gives a unique $c:T\to V$ with $j\circ c=a$. Now $i\circ h\circ c=q\circ a=i\circ b$, and [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism] cancels $i$ to give $h\circ c=b$. Uniqueness already follows from the unique factorization through $j$. This is precisely the universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product]; its uniqueness clause makes the canonical map $V\to W\times_{W^{\prime}}U$ an isomorphism with the required projections.

source.place: Tag 0247, lemma-quasi-affine, proof, final paragraph: stable open is the inverse image of a subset, fpqc quotient topology, and the resulting open-subscheme model; returned proof steps 8, 9 and 10 (open-model part)

proof.text: For the additional base-change presentation, put $f:V\to A$ for the second projection of $\theta\circ j$. Since $\theta$ identifies $q$ with the first projection, the maps $h,f$ agree over $B$, giving $e=(h,f):V\to U\times_B A$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Conversely let $P=U\times_B A$ with projections $u,a$. The pair $(i\circ u,a)$ gives $P\to W^{\prime}\times_B A$, hence $w:P\to W$ using $\theta^{-1}$, and $q\circ w=i\circ u$. Step 4 gives $c:P\to V$ with $j\circ c=w$ and $h\circ c=u$. The $A$-projection of $\theta\circ j\circ c$ is $a$, so $f\circ c=a$. The two product projections give $e\circ c=1_P$; the $W$-projection gives $j\circ c\circ e=j$, so [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism] gives $c\circ e=1_V$. Thus $e$ is the asserted isomorphism over both $U$ and $A$.

source.place: Tag 0247, lemma-quasi-affine, proof, final paragraph: stable open is the inverse image of a subset, fpqc quotient topology, and the resulting open-subscheme model; returned proof steps 8, 9 and 10 (open-model part)

proof.text: Finally put $A_2=A\times_B A$. Pulling the presentation of Step 5 back by either projection $A_2\to A$ identifies each pullback of $V$ with $U\times_B A_2$: a morphism into either object is exactly a pair of maps into $U,A_2$ agreeing over $B$, by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Under these identifications the canonical datum is the identity on $U\times_B A_2$, as in [def-pd-descent-datum]. Write $k:U\times_B A_2\to W^{\prime}\times_B A_2$ for the map induced by $i$. This map is monic: equality after $k$ gives equality of the $A_2$-components and, by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism] for $i$, equality of the $U$-components, hence equality by the product universal property. The hypothesis that $\theta\circ j$ intertwines the given datum with the ambient canonical datum says exactly that the transported $\phi$ satisfies $k\circ\phi=k$. Cancel $k$ to get $\phi=1$. Consequently $e$ identifies the actual given datum, not merely its underlying scheme, with the canonical datum of $U\times_B A$.
